decision: Start with MNIST dataset, then move to CIFAR-10
rationale: Establish the full end-to-end flow with a simpler dataset first. MNIST is 28x28 grayscale (1 channel) vs CIFAR-10's 32x32 RGB (3 channels). This reduces the im2col complexity and weight count for initial verification.

decision: Start with 4x4 systolic array, parameterize to scale to 8x8
rationale: 4x4 (16 PEs) is debuggable by hand. Manual verification of 4x4 matrix multiply is feasible. Parameterized Verilog makes scaling to 8x8 a one-line change. Shows design methodology in portfolio (verified small → scaled up).

decision: Simulation-first approach, deploy to hardware later
rationale: Removes all board-dependency from initial development. All bugs can be caught in simulation with cocotb + Verilator. Board is TBD anyway (arriving in 2-3 days).
alternatives_considered: Buy board first, develop on hardware

decision: Hand-crafted Verilog RTL (no HLS, FINN, or Vitis AI)
rationale: Portfolio impact: shows deep understanding of hardware design. TUM/RWTH value from-scratch implementations over tool-generated black boxes.
alternatives_considered: Use Vitis HLS for faster development
impact: All rtl/ files, project complexity, timeline

rationale: Simplest to implement — weights loaded once into PEs and stay put. Activations stream through. Good match for CNN inference where same weights are reused across many inputs.

decision: Multi-agent coding workflow: Flash (write) → Pro (audit) → Opus (final review)
rationale: Leverages different model strengths. Flash is fast for boilerplate. Pro catches bugs and improves code quality. Opus ensures architectural correctness. Context managed via PROJECT_CONTEXT.md and condense_context.py.

decision: Accept Shaurya's folder structure: sim/ for Verilog testbenches, synth/ for synthesis scripts. Keep verification/ for Adi's cocotb Python tests.
rationale: sim/ and synth/ are standard FPGA/ASIC naming conventions. verification/ contains different content (cocotb Python tests vs Verilog testbenches). Both conventions coexist without conflict. No need to force Shaurya to restructure.

decision: 3-branch git workflow: main (stable), dev (Adi's software), hw-dev (Shaurya's hardware). Weekly review merges both into main.
rationale: Clear ownership prevents merge conflicts. Adi owns model/, verification/, driver/. Shaurya owns rtl/, sim/, synth/. No overlapping files. Weekly ./weekly script fetches both branches for Opus Overseer review before merging.
impact: Git workflow, weekly review script, GIT_STRATEGY.md
